en: Aoooooo<FG> Leave it to us<FG> We'll soon sniff him out<FG>
Why, what considerate little dears you are<FG> My no-good son could do with taking a leaf or two out of both your books<FG>
If you could track him down and bring him back to me, I'd be ever so grateful<FG>
Ohhh, my poor heart... Just where has that little scamp disappeared to<FG><FH>
Any ideas how we'll find this missing boy<FH> His mother thinks he might have left Accordia, but that leaves six whole realms to search...
Just the one, actually. Unless I'm very much mistaken, we'll find him in the pyramid in Dunisia.
The pyramid<FH> But...how could you possibly know that<FH>
Pah, easy-peasy<FG> I asked the lady to give me a handkerchief with her son's scent on it, and had Ruff here give it a sniff.
Yeah<FG> And I found the same smell over by the entrance to the Grand Dunes<FG> My nose never lies<FG>
When I told the lady what we'd found, she said her son was always going on about wanting to visit the pyramids in Dunisia.
Why anyone would want to go poking their nose around a musty old tomb, I'll never know... Boys will be boys, I suppose<FG>
If that's true, then his mother was right to worry<MV>the pyramid's riddled with dangerous monsters, inside and out.
Aoooooo<FG> Then we'd better get over there and get him before something else does<FG>
Is it true<FH> Has my little boy really run off to Dunisia<FH> Please, you've got to rescue him before it's too late<FG>
Thank you so much<FG> My son and his little friend have returned safe and sound<FG>
So they both came straight back, eh<FH> I thought they might do a bit more adventuring on the way...
I wouldn't have put it past them. Listen here, you little scamp<MV>don't you ever run off like that again, or there'll be hell to pay, you hear<FH>
Ahhh, don't be such a worryguts, Mum<FG> We survived, didn't we<FH> Next time we go exploring, we'll be more careful, I promise<FG>
Grrr<FG> What part of ‘don't go off on your own again’ don't you understand<FG><FH> You nearly gave your poor mother a heart attack<FG>
We're all very impressed with how much you love adventuring, but until you can protect yourself and your little friend, no pyramids<FG>
It's all fun and games until someone gets hurt<FG> Do you want to drive your mother into an early grave<FH> Well<MV>do you<FH>
N-No... I'm sorry... I won't go back, I promise. Not until I'm tough like you<FG>
If I'm gonna be the bestest adventurer this world's ever seen, I better get training<FG> See ya later<FG>
Hurf hurf hurf<FG> He's full of beans, isn't he<FH> Looks like that stuff you said to him really hit home<FG>
Pah<FG> I'll believe it when I see it. Those two are every bit as adventure-obsessed as a certain other pair of idiots we know...
Heh, yeah... Hang on<MV>what pair of idiots<FH>
Oh, for heaven's sake<FG> Only our oldest friends, you massive numbskull<FG>
Anyway, all this is making me miss Pilchard Bay. Come on<MV>let's drag this world out of the mess it's in so we can go home.
Ah, heck... I've really gone and done it this time...
I...can't help noticing that something's troubling you. Perhaps I might be able to offer some advice<FH>
Well, alright... It's my big brother<MV>he left the house last night, and he hasn't come back. I think he might have run away from home...
We had an argument, you see. My brother can be pretty self-centred. He always acts like the world revolves around him...
Usually it doesn't really bother me, but this time, I just snapped<MV>I really let him have it. He stormed out, and I haven't seen him since.
Arey... So the put-upon younger sibling finally bit back, is that about the size of it<FH>
That's one way of putting it. I never meant for us to fall out, but the rotten rogue took my<MV><FG> ...No, there's no point going over old wounds.
I just want to know that he's okay. I'm worried he might have gone and got himself into some sort of trouble...
I know exactly how you must feel. Come along, Sis. We must do all we can to reunite this man with his beloved brother.
Oof<FG> Why in the world would we want to do that<FH>
Firstly, because my powers may be the only way to find him, and secondly...let's just say I sympathise with this man's predicament...
Well, if you insist. It's the least I can do for my dear, dear little sister<FG>
Very well<MV>you must leave it to us<FG> We will search for your brother and make sure he comes back to you safe and sound<FG>
Y-You'd really do that for me<FH> Oh, thank you<FG> How could I possibly refuse such a kind offer<FH>
(sigh) Oh, brother... Where are you<FH>
The cards tell me that the man we are searching for is somewhere in the Great Divide.
Are you joking with me<FG><FH> It must have been one heck of an argument to make him run that far<FG>
Indeed... I wonder what our friend's brother could have done to have made him so angry...
Well, he said he took his...something, wasn't it<FH> But what<FH> What could have made him so mad<FH>
...Ah, but of course<FG> When two men argue, it's only ever over one thing<MV>I'll bet a hundred gold coins a girl's involved<FG>
Oh, honestly, Sis<FG> This is hardly the time to be making up stories about strangers<FG>
We need to get to the Great Divide as quickly as we can<MV>if the cards are to be believed, this man may be in terrible danger<FG>
Has my brother really gone all the way to the Great Divide<FH> Ohhh, I hope he's alright...
Ah, you're back<FG> I wanted to thank you for saving my brother from that monster. He told me all about what happened.
It was nothing, honestly. All that matters is that your dear brother is safe and sound. So...are things okay between you now<FH>
Oh, yes<FG> I'm not angry with him any more<MV>I'm just thankful he's alive<FG>
Bruv... You should be angry wiv me<MV>I deserve it. When these girls saved me, I swore I'd say sorry, an' do wot I can to make it up to ya<FG>
So...I'm sorry. I'm sorry I nicked yer life savings an' blew 'em all at the casino<FG>
You gambled away your own brother's savings<FG><FH> Arey, that's awful<FG>
Pfft<FG> All this drama over a few boring old gold coins<FH> I was hoping for some juicy girl-related gossip<FG>
Honestly, Sis<FG> There is nothing ‘boring’ about stealing somebody's hard-earned money<FG> It is a very serious breach of trust<FG>
I know exactly how angry this gentleman must have been<MV>just as angry as I was when you spent all our money on the slot machines<FG>
Oh, please<FG> You're really going to drag that up again<FH> Whatever happened to letting bygones be bygones<FH>
Wot, you ran off wiv yer sister's savings an' all, eh<FH> Hur hur hur<FG> You two are just like me an' me bruv<FG>
Listen... I don't want to fight with you like this ever again. We'll always be brothers...but can we start being friends<FH>
You got it, bruv<FG> Us siblings've gotta stick togevver<FG>
I'm glad they've managed to make up and everything...but I still don't see how a little bit of money can cause such a to-do.
(sigh) Maybe one day you'll understand, Maya. ...Maybe. Sisters, eh<FH> Who'd have one<FH>
Ohhhhhh... (sigh)
My word<FG> Something tells me you're not having a good day. Anything you want to tell us<FH>
Well... Alright, then. It's my girlfriend, you see<MV>I've decided to grasp the nettle and ask her to marry me.
That's wonderful news<FG> So what are you sighing about<FH> Worried she's going to turn you down or something<FH>
Oh, no<MV>we're very much in love. The problem is her family. They're dead against us being together. Especially that dad of hers...
I'm so desperate to spend the rest of my life with her, but I just know the old tyrant's going to say no<FG> Ach, maybe I should just give up...
An excellent idea. Give up and move on with your life.
Angelo<FG> How can you be so cold<FH>
‘Love conquers all’, isn't that what they say<FH> And yet here you are, hesitating because of a little obstacle like an angry father<FH>
If you were as besotted with this woman as you claim, you would never let such a trifle stand between you.
You're right... I've been thinking about this all wrong...
I can't let the old bully scare me off<FG> If he won't step aside and let us be happy, I'll just have to shove him out of the way<FG>
...You wouldn't come with me, would you<FH> I think you might be the moral support I need.
Ugh, Goddess, no. If there's one thing I can't stand, it's sentimental scenes...
Angelo<FG> You can't talk someone into asking the biggest question of all and then leave them in the lurch<FG> What kind of knight are you<FG><FH>
Oh, very well. I'll come along. ...If I must.
Oh, thank you<FG> It's decided, then<MV>I'm going to pop the question if it's the last thing I do<FG>
I want to go and see my girlfriend right away, but the road to Ingenia's teeming with moaning, groaning, walking corpses...
Just thinking about those horrible things makes my skin crawl<FG> Brrr<FG> You couldn't get rid of them for me, could you<FH>
You cleared all the walking corpses out of the Lumberlands for me<FG> Thank you so much<FG>
Hmph<FG> Whatever happened to love conquering all<FH> You can't even visit this would-be wife of yours without calling for reinforcements<FG>
I, I'm sorry... I just can't cope with those creepy creatures. I only have to catch sight of one, and I faint dead away...
That's enough about your...infirmities. The path to Ingenia is clear<MV>it's time to go and get down on one knee<FG>
Y-Yes<FG> Well, that is... Actually...I'm starting to have second thoughts about this whole thing...
I mean<MV>what if she turns me down<FH> I think my heart might actually break...
Hold on a minute<FG> You're not thinking of giving up at the final hurdle, are you<FH>
If you're going to throw in the towel, do it quickly so we can go home. But if I were you, I'd feel more than a little pathetic for doing so.
After all, which is worse<MV>to risk a moment of rejection, or guarantee a lifetime of regret<FH>
...Y-You're right<FG> Thanks, Angelo<FG> Yes<FG> You're so right<FG>
I've got to tell her how I really feel<FG> And even if she doesn't feel the same way about me, at least I'll know for sure<FG>
Right<MV>I'm ready to do this<FG> I hope I can count on your help for just a little longer<FG>
My girlfriend works at the palace in Ingenia, but I'm not brave enough to head there alone. Would you mind coming with me<FH>
Well, he was a right royal pain in the neck if ever I met one...
You're not wrong there. I wonder what happened after we left. Do you think his girlfriend said yes<FH>
Jessica<FG> Angelo<FG>
There's a letter for you. The sender hasn't written their name. Here, take a look.
Jessica opens the letter.
Let's see... ‘Dear Jessica and Angelo,\nShe said yes<FG> I'm getting married, and it's all thanks to you<FG>’
This must be from our young friend<FG> Thank goodness<MV>it sounds like everything worked out well in the end.
Hm<FH> Is that a portrait he's enclosed with the letter<FH> Let's see what kind of woman would agree to marry a man like that, shall we...
.........Bwaaahahahahahaaa<FG> Oh, this is simply priceless<FG>
Let me have a look... Eh<FG><FH> Why would he send a picture of a float-o-copier and a mandrake major...umm...kissing<FH>
Don't you see, Jessica<FH> That faint-hearted fellow was a float-o-copier in disguise<MV>and this lady lizard is his blushing bride-to-be<FG>
Goodness me... A float-o-copier getting married to a mandrake major... That's...quite something...
But what would he want with a great big lizardy girl like that<FH> They're hardly a good match...
Hm. Love is, and always will be, blind, my dear. When you finally fall for someone, you'll learn that for yourself.
Perhaps I could offer my services on that front<FH>
Bring your services anywhere near my front and I'll cut them off, you floppy-haired choirboy<FG>
Fie upon my feebleness<FG> Is there nothing I can do...<FH>
Please to pardon my interjection, but you appear most perturbed. Is there a means in which we can be of relief<FH>
It isn't me who needs helping, it's my wife. She was kidnapped on the day of our wedding, and hasn't been seen since, you see.
The very moment we finished saying our vows, a band of brigands stormed the chapel and carried her away<FG>
Goddess<FG> To confiscate blushing bride on espousal day is a crime beyond comparison<FG>
And one that will incur a punishment of pummellings<FG> These brutes must to be captured, and your bride repossessed without delay<FG>
That's all very well for you to say, but you haven't seen their leader. His biceps are bigger than my head<FG> He'd snap me like a twig<FG>
I don't know anyone tough enough to take him on. But unless I can find someone, I'll never get her back...
Fear not, friend<MV>your search is concluded<FG> I will be overjoyed to belabour this many-muscled man for your behalf<FG>
Are you serious<FH> I don't mean to be rude, but if a girl like you fought an axe-wielding maniac like him, I can only see one outcome...
Please to reconsider<FG> This is Tsarevna Alena, many-crowned mistress of martial arts<FG> She is consuming bandits for morning meal<FG>
And if still you doubt her capability, know that I, Kiryl, shall accompany her on this quest. Your lady spouse is as good as recovered<FG>
Well...if you're sure. It's very kind of you to offer. Maybe the Goddess sent you to help me by way of a wedding present...
And who am I to refuse the will of the heavens<FH> Very well<MV>I leave my darling's deliverance in your capable hands<FG>
I'm no fighter, but I swear I'll do all I can to bring back my beloved. I'll set about tracking down those bandits forthwith<FG>
Come, Kiryl<FG> We must to vigorously penalise these wicked wife-nappers without hesitation<FG>
Yes, Tsarevna, we must<FG> But I fear we cannot do so until their location is unearthed...
Tsarevna Alena<FG> Sir Kiryl<FG>
I've been gathering information about the bandits, and I think I've tracked down their hideout<MV>it's at the top of Mt Neverest<FG>
Neverest...<FH> This is name of tallest mountain in all of your Seven Realms, yes<FH> It is able to be seen even from Accordia.
For why would kidnappers construct hideout in such cold and snowy place<FH> Are there yetis now among their ranks, perhaps<FH>
I don't know about yetis, but rumour has it the leader of the bandits has recruited quite a number of monsters as henchmen.
By all accounts, they're a bloodthirsty bunch. Please, be on your guard.
No foe is sufficiently formidable to resist my fists<FG> I shall batter and belt them with supreme swiftness<FG>
Come, Kiryl<MV>let us make with haste to Mt Neverest. We must to liberate this lady from her icy imprisonment<FG>
I've traced the bandits who kidnapped my bride to the top of Mt Neverest. I beg you<MV>bring her back safely<FG>
Thank you, thank you<FG> You've brought my bride back to me safe and sound<FG>
If you hadn't arrived when you did, goodness knows what would have become of me. I can't thank you enough for coming to my rescue.
Please to not concern yourself<FG> We are merely thankful you were capable to escape unblemished.
Indeed so<FG> And if not for your husband's spirited accumulation of hearsay, we may have failed to discover you with such swiftness.
Th-There's no need to pretend I was anything but useless... I should have been the one fighting, not the one gathering gossip...
But I swear that I will train every day from now on until I'm strong enough to protect you<FG> ...Until then, can you accept me the way I am<FH>
Of course I can, my darling<FG> My heart is yours until my dying day<FG>
Tee hee<FG> Regard them, Kiryl<MV>are they not a superlative couple<FH>
Indeed, yes. I foresee a lengthy and cheer-filled life of matrimony before them.
A life of matrimony, hm<FH> Will I ever to experience such an existence, I ponder...<FH>
B-But, of course you will, Tsarevna<FG> One day, a prince most handsome will surely...
...Aga<FG> Why must I to torture myself with such grievous imaginings<FH> (sniff)
Enough of far-flinged future<FG> While I am yet young, I know no existence more joyful than the pummelling of ever mightier foes<FG>
Why squander my time in envisaging life of matrimony when there is training to be done<FH> Yahoooy<FG>
...I, I mean<MV>please to decelerate, Tsarevna<FG> To race with such excessive speed is too much perilous<FG>
A new quest is now available<FG>
Ahhh, don't the forest just feel like home<FG> Right, let's get huntin' for that wood we<MV> Wait, somethin' don't seem right here...
Yeah. I got a bad feeling about this...
Grrrrrr<FG> Blue one... Big one... You back<FG>
Bad monsters...attack forest<FG> Friends...in danger<FG> Me...fight<FG>
Sounds like our scaly pal's got some uninvited guests on his hands. This ain't no time to be huntin' for wood<MV>we got bigger fish to fry<FG>
Then let's turn up the heat<FG> ‘Bad monsters’, huh<FH> We'll see who's bad<FG> Heh. I'm gonna enjoy this...
Heh. It's not how many weapons you wield<MV>it's how you wield them. Another one bites the dust.
Grrrrrr<FG> Blue one... Big one... Thank you<FG>
Take this... Best wood in woods... Reward...for saving friends...
Terry and Carver receive a piece of good wood<FG>
Get a load o' this, Terry, old pal<FG> This stuff's sturdier'n my right leg<FG> I reckon this is just the kinda wood we're lookin' for, ya know<FG>
Well, you're the expert. You think we can fix that bridge with it<FH>
You betcha<FG> C'mon, let's mosey on back to Accordia and give that guy the good news<FG>

W-We know... Sorry. We were playing adventurers in the pyramid and these scary monsters came, so we ran away and hid here...
But now that you've got rid of them, we can finally go home<FG> Thank you, mister<FG> Thank you, miss<FG>
‘Mister’...<FH> I've never been called that before<FG> I think I like it<FG> Hurf hurf hurf<FG>
Ugh, so they weren't even in danger<FG><FH> What a load of fuss about nothing<FG> Go on<MV>go home to your mothers, you little troublemakers<FG>
Okay<FG> Thanks, miss<FG> Thanks, mister<FG> You really saved our bacon<FG>
Come on, after them. They'll only go getting into more mischief otherwise. Honestly, what kind of child just runs off like that<FH>
I-Is it all over...<FH> Hur hur hur<FG> That'll learn ya, ya flippin' great fleabag<FG> Nobody tries to eat me an' gets away wiv it<FG>
Grrr<FG> You silly, silly man<FG> Who do you think you are, acting so high and mighty<FG><FH> All you did was run away<FG>
Alright, don't get yer knickers in a twist<FG> I was only jokin', weren't I<FH> I know I owe ya one. I'd've been cat food wivout your 'elp<FG>
All that matters is that you are safe now. Come, let us return to Accordia. Your brother has been very worried about you.
Yes, yes. He's very sorry for whatever it was you were fighting about, so hurry up and run along home. And apologise, or else<FG>
Yer right... I'd better say sorry for bein' such a berk, 'adn't I...<FH>
Well, ain't no time like the present<FG> I'm gonna get back to Accordia as quick as me legs'll carry me<FG> Smell ya later, you lot<FG>
...And off he goes again. Ugh, will he ever stop running away<FH>
There's only one way to find out. Come on, Sis<MV>let's follow him back to Accordia and see if he and his brother have made friends again.
